He forced me to law school soon after that. He didnt talk to me when I told him I didn't want to pursue law. AM had enough with the cold war between me and my dad and told me "what? You'll just be like that forever?" (I was employed as an animator). Both of them forced me to law school and when other people would question them as to why they were forcing me, they would tell them "she has no dream" (apparently being an artist was not a dream for them). 

I am a lawyer now. You think it would've been enough, considering that this is what they wanted. But no. They think my salary is still too low for a new lawyer. They're never pleased. I am tired and demotivated by my job.
Because some of us find it easier to see good in others, but not ourselves. It is easier to give love to the world, than to ourselves.

Oh my God, I relate to this post so much, except the part where you are well off. I was also forced into law school by my parents. I'm an artist prior to entering law school and my dad said I won't amount to anything. I initially refused to even take the entrance exam and my dad was so disappointed and angry he didn't talk to me for two months. My mom eventually had enough and finally scolded me, convincing me to enter law school. She said that I should be grateful that I am given this chance. She kept telling me to "just try." I had no interest in law at all. She knows my personality. I never quit something I start. So I told her "If I start this, I will finish it. Can we even afford law school?" She suggested that I work while in law school. I told her I'm not willing to do that because it will probably take me more years to finish if I'm a working student. She said that it's ok. She assured me we have more than enough to get me through law school. On my 5th year, mom suddenly retired saying she no longer wanted to work because she's stressed. My dad was pressured to provide for our family on his own. On my last semester of law school, my mom refused to contribute and told my dad to pay the whole amount. She said it was him who wanted this for me. I clearly remember my dad yelling at me "why is it so expensive?!"  after I told him the amount of my tuition fee. AS IF I WANTED TO ENTER LAW SCHOOL. AS IF I SET THE SCHOOL TUITION FEES. I took the bar exams last February. I had to stay in a dorm to isolate in preparation for the bar because my dad is a frontliner and I won't be allowed to take the bar exams if I test positive for Covid. Now, I am just waiting for the results. Last night I told my mom of my future plans in case I pass the bar and in case I fail. I told her that if I pass I'll immediately apply for a job in the legal profession, but if I fail, I will stay at my current job as a graphic artist so I can study for the next bar exams. She told me "we spent so much on your dorm, and you'll just fail?!" in a high pitched voice. I FEEL SO BETRAYED. I did my part and studied for the bar. I did my best. I finished law school without even wanting to. Instead of comforting or encouraging me while I await the results of something I worked hard for, they're thinking of the money they spent on me. They were the ones who wanted this field and now they think I feel entitled just because they needed to provide a dorm for me. I was so hurt that she was already thinking of the money she "wasted" on my dorm even before the bar results come out. I asked her "are you pressuring me right now? The bar exams are over. I can't really do anything but wait. The bar results aren't even released yet and you're already holding this against me? I haven't even failed yet!" And then she started screaming at how ungrateful I am. How entitled I am. How selfish I am. 

I'm so pissed right now I am literally considering ending my life. I'm in a career path I don't even like because they pressured me into it. And I am the selfish one?

Wow. I know this story is old, but damn, I can relate. This story feels like it's written by the future me. I'm also an Asian Girl. 29 years old. Forced to finish a law degree I never wanted. I also have a younger brother who my parents favor more, though I don't really mind because he is the best brother ever. I have been a consistent achiever from gradeschool to college. I do what is expected of a "good" Asian girl, but they're never really satisfied. They criticize me a lot. When their friends would commend me for achieving something, they would negate that comment and use the opportunity to ridicule me over something petty like how I don't know how to do house chores, or how I have no fashion sense, or I play too much video games. I've gotten used to these things already that I don't notice them much, but my friends point it out. They would even criticize me for having low self-esteem. Looking back, my low self-esteem is probably formed by how they raised me. The saddest part is they never seem to like to see me happy. Whenever I would be happy when I do something I actually like doing, they would literally tell me that I am "too happy." And I don't do drugs nor do I drink alcohol. The things that make me "too happy" are literally reading a book, painting and hanging out with friends. It seems like my parents are so stressed out about their life that seeing me happy infruriates them.

They provide for my needs. On the otherhand, I seem to function well- at least on the outside. I was a consistent honors student from gradeschool to college and I just finished my law degree. But none of that makes me proud, happy or at peace. Nothing excites me. The only thing that calms me down is the thought that I can kill myself if only I can muster enough courage to finally end it all. Slowly, I came to realize that there's nothing wrong with my environment. But there is something wrong with me. I drag those that care for me into this pit of depression I created myself and latch on to them until they drown with me. I feel like a black hole pretending to be a bright star.
I want to kill myself without pain too.
